    Michkov scores twice, Flyers hold off Avalanche

    Zegras has three assists, Woll makes 24 saves for Philadelphia

    By Adam Kimelman
    @NHLAdamK NHL.com Deputy Managing Editor
    October 19, 2026
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 15:23
    Instaread

    PHILADELPHIA -- Matvei Michkov scored two goals, and the Philadelphia Flyers held on for a 3-2 win against the Colorado Avalanche at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Monday.

    It was Philadelphia's second straight victory after losing its first nine games to start the season.

    "I just saw a lot of buy-in tonight," Flyers coach Rick Tocchet said. "We asked certain things from the team, and we're slowly getting more and more of it."

    COL@PHI: Michkov pounces on the loose puck for PPG and 1-0 lead

    Making the victory even more impressive was the fact that the Flyers did it with five injured regulars out of the lineup: forwards Travis Konecny (lower body), Owen Tippett (upper body) and Tyson Foerster (undisclosed), and defensemen Cam York (upper body) and Rasmus Ristolainen (upper body).

    In their place were four rookies: defenseman Hunter McDonald, who was recalled from Lehigh Valley of the American Hockey League on Sunday, and forwards Alex Bump, Cole Knuble and Jacob Gaucher, who were called up from the AHL on Monday.

    "I think it's really important that anyone can be substituted in the lineup and come and play how we need them to," goaltender Joseph Woll said. "You've got guys playing bigger roles, and the guys coming into the lineup, for me, it seems like we didn't take a step down at all from our systems and honestly elevated our play. So, it was pretty cool to see from my vantage point."

    Noel Acciari scored his first goal of the season, and Trevor Zegras had three assists for Philadelphia (2-6-3), which began the season 0-6-3 before defeating the Ottawa Senators 3-1 on Saturday. Woll made 24 saves.

    Martin Necas and T.J. Hughes scored for Colorado (5-3-1). Mackenzie Blackwood made 21 saves.

    "Sluggish and sloppy," Avalanche coach Jared Bednar said. "Execution was a big factor for us tonight, and the pace we were playing at. Sloppy, and passes weren't good, handling passes wasn't good. It's hard to go anywhere when you're beating the puck up, and that's what I thought we did for the bulk of the game."

    Michkov scored a power-play goal to give the Flyers a 1-0 lead at 7:41 of the first period. He received the puck in the right corner and passed across to Zegras, whose slap-pass hit Flyers forward Denver Barkey in front before popping back out to Michkov, who shot into an open net from below the right circle.

    The goal stood after the Avalanche challenged the play for goaltender interference.

    Michkov then made it 2-0 at 12:23 of the second period. He circled the offensive zone before scoring with a shot from above the circles that went through traffic and past Blackwood.

    "Those goals are just goal-scorers' goals," Tocchet said. "He's timing it right, because sometimes you overshoot it or you're too late, but he has a knack to do that. So, he's skating well."

    COL@PHI: Michkov scores his second goal of the game

    Michkov has scored in three straight games, including back-to-back games with a power-play goal. He leads the Flyers with six goals in 11 games; it took him 22 games to score six last season.

    "I feel good," Michkov said. "I feel so good on ice, and I think I have energy for the season. I want to play and I want to support the team more."

    Necas scored three seconds after a power play expired to make it 2-1 at 17:52. Artturi Lehkonen found Necas open above the right face-off circle, and he roofed a shot through traffic over Woll's blocker.

    Acciari pushed the Flyers' lead to 3-1 at 6:34 of the third period, redirecting Oliver Bonk's slap shot from the right point. It was Acciari's first point in 11 games with the Flyers.

    Hughes cut it to 3-2 14:40 of the third. Sam Malinski's shot from the right point deflected off the stick of teammate Fedor Svechkov to Hughes, who scored from the right face-off circle.

    Blackwood was pulled for an extra attacker with 2:02 remaining in the third, but the Avalanche generated just one shot on goal and had three attempts blocked, all by Flyers defenseman Travis Sanheim.

    "I don't think we were our sharpest," Avalanche defenseman Josh Manson said. "I just think we weren't sharp tonight. ... I think maybe we found our game a little too late."

    NOTES: It's the third time Michkov has scored in three straight games, and he has five points (four goals, one assist) during a three-game point streak. He's also the first Flyer to score a power-play goal in consecutive games since Konecny on Dec. 31, 2024, and Jan. 2, 2025. ... Zegras had his fourth three-assist NHL game, and his first in two seasons with the Flyers. ... It's the first game the Flyers have scored three times against a goalie this season. Their third goal against the Senators was an empty-net goal. ... Knuble had one shot on goal in 13:44 of ice time in his NHL debut. ... Lehkonen has five points (three goals, two assists) during a four-game point streak.
